nodes.label: HBM contract prices (TrendForce)
nodes.relation: Tracks what NVIDIA pays for the HBM stacked on every data center GPU
nodes.summary: TrendForce's HBM price outlook is the biggest single input-cost read for NVIDIA's gross margin in 2027.
brief: HBM is the largest bought-in cost on a Rubin GPU, so its price hits margin first.
nodes.health: Forecasts 2027 blended HBM prices up 121% on 2026, with supply still tight.
nodes.tracks: Gross margin, through the price of the HBM memory NVIDIA buys
nodes.reading: September 29, 2026: 2027 blended HBM ASP forecast raised to up 121% year on year; market stays supply-constrained in 2027
nodes.cadence: Forecast updates every one to two months
nodes.leads: Two to four quarters ahead of gross margin, since 2027 contracts set the memory cost of Rubin systems

nodes.label: DRAM contract prices (TrendForce)
nodes.relation: Tracks the price of conventional server and mobile DRAM that goes into NVIDIA's rack systems
nodes.summary: Conventional DRAM contract prices are still rising every quarter, which is the cost NVIDIA blamed for its lower margin guide.
brief: NVIDIA says memory prices rose faster than it expected and set its margin bottom.
nodes.health: Conventional DRAM contract prices forecast up 10-15% in 4Q26 after larger earlier gains.
nodes.tracks: Gross margin, through the cost of the CPU-side memory in each rack
nodes.reading: September 30, 2026: conventional DRAM contract prices forecast up 10-15% quarter on quarter in 4Q26; server DRAM stays undersupplied
nodes.cadence: Quarterly forecast plus monthly contract price bulletins
nodes.leads: About one to two quarters ahead of reported gross margin

nodes.label: SK hynix
nodes.relation: Main HBM supplier for NVIDIA's data center GPUs
nodes.summary: SK hynix's own results show how much pricing power the memory makers hold over NVIDIA going into 2027.
brief: Its record margins are partly NVIDIA's memory bill, so its pricing power caps NVIDIA's margin.
nodes.health: 3Q26 operating profit was 83.33 trillion won on 104.62 trillion won revenue, about 80%.
nodes.tracks: Gross margin, through what the largest HBM supplier can charge
nodes.reading: October 28, 2026: 3Q26 revenue 104.62 trillion won, up 327.89% year on year; DRAM and HBM volumes effectively sold out through 2029
nodes.cadence: Quarterly, about four weeks after quarter end
nodes.leads: One quarter or more ahead of NVIDIA's gross margin, since its contract prices become NVIDIA's cost

nodes.label: TSMC wafer and CoWoS pricing
nodes.relation: The price NVIDIA pays TSMC to make and package each GPU
nodes.summary: Reported TSMC price notices for 2027 add a second cost push on top of memory.
brief: Wafer and CoWoS price hikes raise the cost of every NVIDIA GPU next year.
nodes.health: Reported weighing CoWoS hikes up to 20% and wafer increases of 3-6% from January 2027.
nodes.tracks: Gross margin, through wafer and advanced packaging costs
nodes.reading: October 27, 2026 reports: TSMC weighing CoWoS price hikes of up to 20%; wafer prices up 3-6% from January 2027 depending on node
nodes.cadence: Irregular; price notices for the next year usually surface in the second half
nodes.leads: Two to three quarters ahead of gross margin

nodes.label: Dell'Oro AI back-end switch tracker
nodes.relation: Ranks vendors of the Ethernet switches that connect GPUs inside AI clusters
nodes.summary: Dell'Oro shows NVIDIA close behind Celestica's white-box switches in AI back-end Ethernet, so Spectrum-X is not winning every cluster.
brief: Shows whether Spectrum-X is winning the scale-out Ethernet that drives networking revenue.
nodes.health: Back-end switch sales passed front-end sales for the first time in 2Q26.
nodes.tracks: Networking revenue, through NVIDIA's share of AI back-end Ethernet switching
nodes.reading: 2Q26 (published September 3, 2026): Celestica led Ethernet AI back-end switch sales, NVIDIA a close second, Arista third, Cisco gained the most share
nodes.cadence: Quarterly, about two months after quarter end; 3Q26 report likely in December
nodes.leads: Confirms share about one quarter after NVIDIA reports networking revenue

nodes.label: IDC data center Ethernet switch tracker
nodes.relation: Measures NVIDIA's Spectrum-X Ethernet switch revenue against Arista and Cisco
nodes.summary: IDC puts NVIDIA at the top of data center Ethernet switching, though its share slipped a point between 1Q26 and 2Q26.
brief: The cleanest outside count of Spectrum-X sales, a growing part of networking revenue.
nodes.health: Data center Ethernet switching reached $12.3B in 2Q26, up 64.5% year on year.
nodes.tracks: Networking revenue, through NVIDIA's Ethernet switch sales and share
nodes.reading: 2Q26 (published September 11, 2026): NVIDIA $2.5B, up 181.1% year on year, 20.4% share, down from 21.5% in 1Q26
nodes.cadence: Quarterly, about ten weeks after quarter end
nodes.leads: Lags NVIDIA's report by a quarter but splits out Ethernet, which NVIDIA no longer does

nodes.label: LandMark Optoelectronics
nodes.relation: Makes laser and photodetector epiwafers that go into data center optical modules
nodes.summary: LandMark's monthly sales are the earliest scheduled read on optics demand for AI scale-out networks.
brief: Its monthly sales show optics demand before the modules ship with NVIDIA networking.
nodes.health: October 2026 sales were NT$570 million, up 183% on last year.
nodes.tracks: Networking revenue, through demand for the lasers inside AI optical modules
nodes.reading: NT$570 million in October 2026, up 5.5% from September and 183.0% from October 2025; January to October up 141.7%
nodes.cadence: Monthly, about five days after month end
nodes.leads: Roughly one to two quarters ahead of optics-heavy networking revenue, as epiwafers become modules

nodes.label: Innolight
nodes.relation: Major maker of the 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers used in AI cluster networks
nodes.summary: Innolight's growth and 1.6T ramp show the optics attached to AI networks are still accelerating.
brief: Its sales track the optics that ship alongside NVIDIA switches and NICs.
nodes.health: 3Q26 net profit was RMB 8.59 billion, up 174% on last year.
nodes.tracks: Networking revenue, through optical transceiver volumes for AI clusters
nodes.reading: 3Q26 (reported October 31, 2026): revenue RMB 27.8 billion, up 172% year on year; 1.6T revenue growth accelerated
nodes.cadence: Quarterly, within a month of quarter end
nodes.leads: Roughly in step with NVIDIA's networking revenue, reported about three weeks earlier

nodes.label: Street margin consensus
nodes.relation: Analyst expectations NVIDIA's gross margin is judged against
nodes.summary: The street expected 74% for the October quarter and NVIDIA beat it; the step down to 71-72% had been flagged since August.
brief: NVIDIA beat the 74.03% consensus by almost a point last quarter.
nodes.health: Q3 FY27 GAAP gross margin 74.8% versus 74.03% expected.
nodes.tracks: What analysts expect NVIDIA's gross margin to be
nodes.reading: Q3 FY27 GAAP gross margin consensus 74.03% versus 74.8% actual (November 17, 2026); no published consensus found for the Q4 guide
nodes.cadence: Continuously updated; snapshot before each report
nodes.leads: Sets the bar for the February report

signals.headline: NVIDIA reports third-quarter gross margin of 74.9%, above its own 74% guide
signals.whyItMatters: Margin held near 75% even as Rubin started ramping, up 1.4 points on last year, so pricing still covers rising costs.
signals.evidence: GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 74.8% and 74.9%, respectively

signals.headline: NVIDIA guides fourth-quarter gross margin down to 71-72% and calls it the bottom
signals.whyItMatters: A three-point drop from 74.9% is the memory bill showing up; it stays above the 70% kill line, but there is less room than a year ago.
signals.evidence: We expect Q4 to mark the bottom of gross margins before improving to the 72 to 73 range in fiscal year '28.

signals.headline: NVIDIA's supply commitments jump to $390 billion, mostly multi-year memory purchases
signals.whyItMatters: Locking in memory secures Rubin volume, but it also fixes NVIDIA's cost at peak-cycle prices for years.
signals.evidence: supply commitments increased from $279 billion last quarter to $390 billion, primarily related to the multi-year procurement of memory supply

signals.headline: Nvidia Breaks Revenue And Profit Records, And Will Keep Doing It
signals.whyItMatters: Networking is now about a fifth of data center revenue and roughly 2.6 times the $8.2 billion of a year ago, so NVIDIA captures more of each rack.
signals.evidence: Nvidia's networking business brought in more than $21 billion in sales

signals.headline: NVIDIA Q3 FY27 gross margin 74.8% versus 74.03% expected
signals.whyItMatters: Beating the margin bar by almost a point shows memory costs have not yet outrun NVIDIA's pricing.

signals.headline: HBM Supply Constraints Persist, 2027 Price Outlook Revised Upward with Blended ASP Forecast to Rise 121% YoY, Says TrendForce
signals.whyItMatters: HBM more than doubling in price is the main reason NVIDIA's margin steps down, and the FY28 recovery depends on passing it on.
signals.evidence: Blended ASP is now projected to jump 121% YoY.

signals.headline: AI Server Demand Sustains Memory Contract Price Increases in 4Q26, While Consumer-Side Pressure Persists, Says TrendForce
signals.whyItMatters: Another 10-15% rise in conventional DRAM lands in the quarter NVIDIA already guided as its margin low.
signals.evidence: Conventional DRAM contract prices are projected to grow 10–15% QoQ in 4Q26

signals.headline: SK hynix says DRAM and HBM booked through 2029 as profit soars to $62 billion
signals.whyItMatters: A supplier earning about 80% operating margin with volumes sold out to 2029 holds the pricing power, which caps how far NVIDIA's margin can recover.
signals.evidence: our DRAM and HBM volumes for the next three years through 2029 are effectively sold out

signals.headline: TSMC Reportedly Eyes 20% CoWoS Price Hike, Skips Equipment Price Renegotiations Amid AI Demand Surge
signals.whyItMatters: Packaging and wafer hikes in 2027 stack on top of memory, so NVIDIA's own price increases have to cover two cost pushes.
signals.evidence: weighing price hikes of up to 20%

signals.headline: AI back-end network switch sales surpass front-end networks for the first time in 2Q26
signals.whyItMatters: The AI switch market is growing fast, but white-box Celestica still leads and Cisco is gaining, so Spectrum-X share is not guaranteed.
signals.evidence: Celestica retained the leading position, followed closely by NVIDIA

signals.headline: Ethernet Switch Market Surges 43.4% to $18.9B in 2Q26 as AI Infrastructure Demand Drives Record Datacenter Spending
signals.whyItMatters: Spectrum-X nearly tripled its Ethernet sales on last year, though its share slipped from 21.5% to 20.4%, so the growth is the market as much as share gains.
signals.evidence: NVIDIA $2.5B, 20.4% share, up 181.1% year over year

signals.headline: LandMark October revenue NT$570 million, up 183% year on year
signals.whyItMatters: Laser epiwafer sales still rising in October point to optics demand holding into NVIDIA's January quarter.
signals.evidence: 10 月營收,達 5.70 億元,較去年同期成長 183.0%

signals.headline: Innolight third-quarter profit up 174% as 1.6T shipments ramp
signals.whyItMatters: Optics revenue nearly tripling with 1.6T accelerating matches the networking surge NVIDIA reported three weeks later.
signals.evidence: 1.6T產品收入成長加快; revenue 人民幣278億元, up 172% YoY
